question: What is the main goal of safe motherhood programs?

options.A: To shorten the duration of pregnancy
options.B: To reduce maternal and neonatal deaths
options.D: To completely eliminate normal labor pain

explanation: Spot on! Safe motherhood programs are all about keeping both mothers and newborns safe, healthy, and alive. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h1)

question: Why should nurses treat every pregnancy as though complications could happen?

options.A: Routine delivery is considered a surgical emergency
options.B: Standard tests are rarely accurate during gestation
options.C: Complications can occur suddenly without prior warning
options.D: Most pregnant women develop chronic illnesses

explanation: Exactly! Even a smooth pregnancy can change quickly, so staying alert helps us catch issues early and save lives. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h1)

question: How many main pillars make up the core safe motherhood framework?
explanation: That's correct! The four pillars are family planning, antenatal care, safe delivery (obstetric care), and postnatal care. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h2)

question: Which pillar of safe motherhood focuses on checking on the mother and baby right after childbirth?
explanation: Well done! Postnatal care happens after delivery to make sure both mother and baby are recovering smoothly. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h2)

question: Which vaccine is routinely given during pregnancy to protect the newborn from a deadly infection?
explanation: Spot on! Tetanus toxoid is given to expectant mothers to protect their babies from neonatal tetanus. Great memory! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h3)

question: Why must pregnant women attend antenatal clinics even when they feel completely fine?

options.A: To eliminate all potential discomforts of pregnancy
options.B: To prevent the fetus from moving into a breech position
options.C: To detect silent conditions like high blood pressure early
options.D: To guarantee a normal vaginal delivery date

explanation: You got it! Some dangerous issues like high blood pressure don't show early signs, which is why regular clinic checks are so important. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h3)

question: What is the main chart midwives use during labor to track progress and catch problems early?
explanation: Correct! The partograph is a simple yet powerful graphical chart that helps us monitor labor and spot when things are taking too long. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h4)

question: Who is considered a skilled birth attendant?

options.A: A family member who has given birth multiple times
options.B: Any volunteer working at a local health post
options.C: A trained health professional such as a nurse or midwife
options.D: An experienced traditional birth healer in the community

explanation: Spot on! A skilled birth attendant is a certified professional, like a nurse or midwife, trained to manage normal births and handle emergencies. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h4)

question: When is the risk of maternal and newborn complications highest after delivery?
explanation: Exactly! The first 48 hours after birth require our closest attention because heavy bleeding or infections can happen quickly. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h5)

question: You are caring for a mother 2 hours after delivery. Which finding needs your immediate action?

options.A: Moderate fatigue and sleepiness following labor
options.B: Mild cramping pains while the baby is breastfeeding
options.C: A rapidly filling perineal pad with bright red blood

explanation: Well done! Heavy, soaking bleeding is a sign of postpartum hemorrhage—a true emergency that needs quick nursing intervention. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h5)

question: What major service makes a comprehensive emergency obstetric care center different from a basic one?
explanation: Spot on! Comprehensive centers can handle major surgeries like Cesarean sections and blood transfusions when basic care isn't enough. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of emergency obstetric care networks?

options.A: To replace the need for routine antenatal checkups
options.B: To reduce the overall birth rate in rural populations
options.C: To provide long-term family planning counseling
options.D: To treat sudden, life-threatening complications during birth

explanation: Correct! These networks ensure that when a sudden crisis hits during labor, mothers can get life-saving emergency care fast. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h6)

question: Which of these is a key community role for a nurse promoting safe motherhood?
explanation: You got it! Teaching families about danger signs and encouraging them to visit the clinic early is one of our best community tools. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h7)

question: Why is it so important to build trust between pregnant women and nurses?

options.A: It encourages women to seek care early and report complications
options.B: It guarantees that labor will be completely painless
options.C: It prevents the need for any postpartum checkups
options.D: It eliminates all cultural beliefs surrounding childbirth

explanation: Spot on! When women trust us, they feel safe coming to the clinic early and speaking up when something doesn't feel right. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h7)
